agyos_skill.intent: Static and dynamic reverse engineering of binaries, compiled applications, and network protocols. Bridges disassembly engines, decompilation validation, and runtime tracing within AGYOS.
agyos_skill.instructions: An operational guide for inspecting compiled executables, understanding binary architectures, and reverse-engineering proprietary network protocols for security research and interoperability. The analysis pipeline supports native and bytecode targets: - Native Binaries: ELF (Linux), Mach-O (macOS/iOS), PE32/PE32+ (Windows). - Virtual Machine Bytecode: JVM `.class`/`.jar`, .NET CLR assemblies, Dalvik/ART (`.dex`/`.apk`), WebAssembly (`.wasm`). - Disassembly & Decompilation: Ghidra (headless scripting), radare2 / rizin (`r2pipe`), Hopper Disassembler, IDA Free. - Binary Inspection: `readelf`, `objdump`, `nm`, `strings`, `binwalk`, `checksec`. - Dynamic Tracing: Frida (cross-platform JavaScript instrumentation), `strace`, `ltrace`, GDB with GEF/PEDA. - Network Protocol Interception: Wireshark / tshark, mitmproxy (TLS interception). Execute static inspection sequentially before running dynamic processes: 1. Metadata & Hardening Audit: ```bash file target_binary checksec --file=target_binary ``` - Identify architecture (x86_64, ARM64), linking (static vs dynamic), and security mitigations (PIE, stack canaries, NX/DEP, RELRO). 2. String & Symbol Extraction: - Filter readable ASCII/UTF-16 strings with length thresholds: ```bash strings -n 8 target_binary | grep -E "https?://|/api/|key|token|auth" ``` - Export exported/imported symbols via `nm -D` or `readelf -s`. 3. Decompilation & Control Flow Recovery: - Identify main entry points, dispatch tables, and cryptographic primitives. - Trace cross-references (`xrefs`) to sensitive APIs (socket operations, filesystem writes, crypto keys). 1.
